newsitem.title: USA: Vt.treasurer urges 'pay-to-play' bond lawyer ban.
newsitem.headline: Vt.treasurer urges 'pay-to-play' bond lawyer ban.

text.p: Vermont Treasurer James Douglas, in a letter to the state's bar association, is pushing for a five-year ban prohibiting bond lawyers from executing sales if they have made a political contribution to the public official in charge of the bond sale.
Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board regulations, known as "pay-to-play," already prohibit underwriters from making campaign contributions to politicians who select them.
The American Bar Association, meeting in San Francisco, is considering a resolution from the New York City Bar that is similar to the MSRB rules.
In his letter to the Vermont Bar Association, which is also represented at the San Francisco meeting, Douglas urged further reform.

"Vermont law does not allow any financial services firm or those representing financial services firms -- including bond firms and lawyers -- from holding a contract with the treasurer's office if they have contributed to a treasurer's campaign during the last five years," Douglas wrote.
"I would hope that our delegation to the ABA meeting could vote to put more teeth into this resolution and call for action similar to Vermont's law," he wrote.
